source.title: Breaking Language Barriers: Cross-Lingual Continual Pre-Training at Scale
source.authors: Wen-Zheng Zheng; Wenbo Pan; Xun Xu; Li-Bo Qin; Li Yue; Ming Zhou

record.file_problem: The full paper is present. Some equations and figure labels have formatting or OCR artifacts, but the relevant results are readable.
record.tranche_reason: Tests scaling in cross-lingual continual pre-training (CPT), a different training regime from the original from-scratch scaling studies.
record.gate_note: The paper reports held-out loss scaling fits, compute-optimal allocations, and loss outcomes under source-language replay. Downstream benchmark results are reported but do not test downstream predictability with scale or pretraining loss. Literature results cited from other work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study trains 40 LLaMA2-style models (about 50M to 5.5B parameters) on Chinese text, both from scratch and by continual pre-training (CPT) from English checkpoints. It fits held-out loss against compute and against parameters and tokens, and derives compute-optimal allocations. This puts V1 in a new language setting and tests V5 (transfer/CPT regime), V3 and V7 directly.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is mostly right but needs three additions. First, the authors also conclude that CPT preserves the loss-compute power law with a nearly unchanged exponent. Second, they conclude that 5% to 30% source-language replay prevents forgetting without hurting target-language scaling. Third, their claim that CPT 'favors larger models' rests on the allocation prefactor: the CPT parameter exponent (0.385) is actually lower than the scratch one (0.429).
record.recipe_differences: Uses held-out cross-entropy scaling fits and compute-optimal allocation in the general style of prior scaling-law work, but studies English-to-Chinese CPT and introduces an extended joint data-parameter term. It is not a direct reproduction of the original studies.
record.method_sensitivity: The fitted allocation and loss form differ between scratch pre-training and CPT. CPT fit error depends on whether the Chinchilla or extended law is used. Replay ratio changes the early English-loss trajectory, while the text reports matched Chinese loss at equal compute across the tested ratios. The paper also flags hyperparameter, language, and training-duration constraints.

fits_no_version.finding: CPT saves 25% to 50% of FLOPs at matched loss. The saving shrinks over training and is larger for bigger models.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Cross-lingual initialisation gives a compute saving at matched loss that grows with model size and shrinks with training length.

fits_no_version.finding: Chinese loss at equal Chinese-allocated compute is unaffected by English replay ratios from 1% to 80%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Source-data replay does not change target-language loss scaling per unit of target compute.

fits_no_version.finding: Without replay, English loss of the 1.4B model rises from 2.40 to 3.68, and forgetting is worse in smaller models.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Forgetting during cross-lingual CPT decreases with model size.

fits_no_version.finding: At 1.4B, CPT beats scratch training on zero-shot benchmarks in French, Russian and Chinese, with French gaining most.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Cross-lingual CPT downstream gains vary with linguistic similarity to the source language.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing (2024)
record.problems: The authors note that compute and model sizes are limited, experiments use LLaMA2 architecture, hyperparameters were selected through experience and trial and error, and the study does not test over-trained source models or vocabulary extension. Fit uncertainty and confidence intervals are not reported. Some outcomes are shown in figures without exact per-condition values.
record.rows_left_out: No reported result-bearing rows were omitted.

untested.parts: There is no held-out extrapolation. The Figure 5 frontiers out to 1e24 FLOPs are predictions that are never checked against larger runs.
Shape is varied together with size (following Muennighoff et al.). Depth and width are never compared at a fixed parameter count.
Downstream results are reported only at 1.4B (Fig 3, Fig 6). Downstream performance is never related to scale or to loss.
No other modalities, no fine-tuning, and no repeated-data regimes. CPT scaling is measured only for English to Chinese; French and Russian have downstream results only.
There is no direct IsoFLOP or multi-budget empirical test of the optimal N/D. The allocation is only derived from the fitted parametric law.

missing.what: Fitted γ values from the extended law: -0.005 for scratch and 0.080 for CPT. These show the joint term is null for scratch training.
Downstream relative performance at different English replay ratios (1.4B). The authors pick about 30% as optimal.
Unvalidated compute-optimal frontiers extrapolated to 1e24 FLOPs for both strategies.

record.verdict_notes: The model range is stated as 40M–5B in the abstract but 50M–5.5B in Table 1. All models are trained at 20 tokens per parameter with one cosine schedule, so the allocation exponents come from a parametric fit rather than from varied token budgets. No uncertainty is reported on any fit. The CPT fit fixes E, A and α at the scratch values. The study is not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: Tests Chinese-language scratch pre-training and CPT loss scaling, including compute and joint parameter-data fits; does not establish the claimed law across other datasets or broadly beyond the tested scales.
No held-out extrapolation test in which a fit on smaller runs predicts the losses of much larger runs.
Reports fitted compute-optimal parameter and token exponents for scratch pre-training and CPT; does not test the trend across compute budgets beyond the fitted experimental range.
No controlled comparison of depth, width, or other architecture details at fixed parameter count.
Tests cross-lingual CPT and replaying within text pre-training; does not test other modalities, fine-tuning, or transfer regimes beyond this CPT setup.
Reports downstream benchmark performance at one stated model size, but does not test predictability of downstream performance with scale or pretraining loss.
Shows differences between scratch and CPT fitted allocations and compares two fit forms, but does not systematically vary parameter counting, training schedule, data, or fitting procedures.
